name: Kazakhstan
summary_text: Kazakhstan demands real caution from trans visitors — Central Asia's most liveable country for trans people, which is a relative statement. Nothing is criminalised; legal gender recognition exists (heavily medicalised: psychiatric boards, and surgery requirements applied in practice); and revealingly, hundreds of trans people fled TO Kazakhstan from Russia after its propaganda law and LGR ban. ODIHR recorded 62 anti-LGBTI bias incidents in 2024 — real, but documented and reported, which itself indicates functioning civil society (Feminita, ECOM). The trajectory is the concern: a “We Are Against Open and Hidden LGBT Propaganda” petition gained official review by the Ministry of Culture in 2024 (HRW urged rejection), and anti-gender MPs are vocal. Currently there is no propaganda statute, no bathroom law, and no police targeting pattern — police are unhelpful rather than predatory. For a visitor: no legal exposure; low visibility keeps visitor exposure small; Almaty/Astana are navigable.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Kazakhstan: hate crimes and police abuse against LGBTQI people continued - an activist nearly run over by a driver who recognised her (no investigation); a trans sex worker harassed, blackmailed and extorted by police posing as clients; hundreds of trans people reportedly came to Kazakhstan from Russia fleeing the war or 'LGBT propaganda' laws; an employment site initially denied an LGBT NGO's registration; anti-LGBTQI statements by politicians, journalists and religious leaders.
OSCE/ODIHR 2024 Hate Crime Report for Kazakhstan: no data reported to ODIHR since 2018; no National Point of Contact; civil-society reports for 2024 from ALMA-TQ, ECOM, Feminita and others.

sources.title: Kazakhstan Should Reject Attempt to Curtail LGBT People’s Rights | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jul 2024): 'Kazakhstan Should Reject Attempt to Curtail LGBT People's Rights' — the 'LGBT propaganda' bill would further stigmatise and endanger LGBT Kazakhs.

sources.title: Regional Report on Violations of the Human Rights of LGBT People in the Countries of Eastern Europe and Central Asia 2024 - ECOM
sources.claim_summary: ECOM Regional Report 2024 on violations of the human rights of LGBT people in Eastern Europe and Central Asia (Armenia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Ukraine): documented violations of the right to health, barriers faced by LGBT people, and law-enforcement practices, based on monitoring since 2017.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission to International Organizations in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to Kazakhstan's international human-rights environment.

sources.title: Tatler is first Russian glossy magazine to feature a trans cover star
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (March 2020): Tatler made history as the first Russian glossy to feature a trans cover star - Natasha Maximova, born in Kazakhstan to a 'simple but loving family' who believed she was a boy; she identified as a girl from an early age; the Russian 'gay propaganda law' does not extend to gender identity.

sources.title: Kazakhstan Supreme Court Upholds Privacy Rights | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Sept 2019): 'Kazakhstan: Supreme Court Upholds Privacy Rights' - the court's ruling protecting privacy rights, significant in the context of proposed 'propaganda' restrictions targeting LGBT content in Kazakhstan.
